chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad and Abu Ghalib al-Zurari and others, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub. And al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah informed me from a number of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from 'Abd Allah al-Kahili, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, and he said:

"Face the soles of his feet toward the qiblah so that his face is facing the qiblah. Then soften his joints; if they resist you, then leave them. Then begin with his private part using water of sidr and al-hurud, and wash it three washings, using plenty of water, and wipe his abdomen with a gentle wiping. Then move to his head, beginning with his right side from his beard and head, then follow with his left side from his head, beard, and face; wash him gently, beware of harshness, and wash him with a soft washing. Then lay him on his left side so that his right side appears to you, then wash him from the top of his head to his feet, and pass your hand over his back and abdomen with three washings. Then return him onto his right side so that his left side appears to you, then wash him with water from the top of his head to his feet, and pass your hand over his back and abdomen with three washings. Then return him onto the back of his head, and begin with his private part using camphor-water, and do as you did the first time: wash him with three washings using camphor-water and al-hurud, and pass your hand gently over his abdomen. Then move to his head and do as you did first with his beard on both sides, and his head and face, using camphor-water, three washings. Then return him to the left side so that his right side appears to you, then wash him from the top of his head to his feet three washings, and insert your hand beneath his shoulders and his forearms, while the forearm and the hand remain visible alongside his side. Whenever you wash any part of him, insert your hand beneath his shoulders and into the inner side of his forearms. Then return him onto his back, then wash him with pure water as you did at first: beginning with the private part, then move to the head, beard, and face, until you do as you did at first with pure water. Then bind him with the cloth, with cotton beneath it, binding him firmly with abundant cotton. Then tie his thighs over the cotton with the cloth very tightly so that there is no fear that anything may come out. Beware of making him sit or pressing his abdomen, and beware of stuffing anything into his ears. If you fear that something may come out from the nostril, then there is no harm in placing cotton there; but if you do not fear, then place nothing in it. Do not clean beneath his nails, and the ghusl (ritual bath) of the woman is likewise."

key_terms.الْخِرْقَةِ: the cloth used for binding and covering
key_terms.الْقُطْنُ: cotton placed beneath the cloth for protection
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction faced during ritual observance
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.فَرْجِهِ: the private part of the deceased
key_terms.مَاءِ السِّدْرِ: water mixed with lote leaves used in the washing
key_terms.مَاءِ الْقَرَاحِ: pure unmixed water used in the final washing
key_terms.مَاءِ الْكَافُورِ: camphor-water used in one stage of the washing

ai.seo_question: How is the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased performed according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith details the jurisprudential method of performing the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, including orientation toward the qiblah, the order of washing, the substances used, and practical cautions during the process. It emphasizes gentleness, dignity, and procedural care in preparing the dead, and it states that the same ruling applies to the washing of a woman.
